candidates.name: N-consecutive-clean-runs proof standard
candidates.fit_for_gap: goal-3-fix-proof-standard: driver-contract is green 128/128 x4 while the defect persists, so a single passing run certifies nothing for an intermittent (~1/3) defect.
candidates.decision_rationale: Restate Goal 3's gate as N consecutive clean full-run passes. N >= 10 is suggested by the observed ~1/3 failure rate UNDER AN INDEPENDENCE ASSUMPTION (P(10 clean | broken) ~= (2/3)^10 ~= 1.7%); consecutive-run state coupling (orphaned children, lock residue, pipe state, shared caches) inflates the false-negative probability, so (a) a pre-run cleanup step (process-tree kill, scratch-dir reset) is required before the bound applies, and (b) N must be re-sized from the failure rate the cand-2 harness actually measures (assessment: small sample so far). Assessment-derived reasoning lives here because the schema restricts evidence[] to tiers 1-4.

evidence.claim: Flaky-test remediation uses repeat-run statistical criteria, not one-shot pass/fail.
Race conditions / timing issues ranked root cause #1 of flaky tests.
Multivocal review of flaky-test causes and mitigation; timing/order dependence dominant.
Re-run-N-times pattern recommended to distinguish real failures from flakiness.

risks: Run-to-run independence is unproven; the (2/3)^10 bound is optimistic under positive correlation.
N sized from a small observed sample; the harness must measure the true rate before N is fixed.

candidates.name: Instrumented repeat-run reproduction harness
candidates.fit_for_gap: goal-1-blocking-command: the stage-10 call chain is known by reading (run-research.sh:478 -> review_report :340 -> sync_report_status :364 -> write-provenance.sh :365 -> build-review-packet.sh :367 -> judge dispatch :372-377) but no blocking command has been isolated; for an intermittent defect, single-shot instrumentation is insufficient.
candidates.decision_rationale: Build a repeat-run harness looping driver-contract.sh --scenario full-run up to K times (or until hang) with per-call tracing (set -x capture, and/or macOS sample/dtruss of the child process tree) so the first hanging run yields the exact blocked command and its stack, plus output-volume capture at the hang site (to test the ~64 KB pipe-buffer hypothesis). A live capture is the only way to learn which child holds a driver invocation that never returns (assessment open question 1). Also feeds goal-2 dating once the site is known. Off-the-shelf categories were considered and rejected (analysis.md Tier 1-3 negative results). Assessment-derived reasoning lives here because the schema restricts evidence[] to tiers 1-4.

evidence.claim: Timing-dependent defects require repeated execution under instrumentation; single-shot repro is unreliable.
Isolate flaky failures by reproducing under tracing before attempting fixes.

risks: If the hang never reproduces under the harness, the measured-rate plan for cand-1 loses its input; harness must run enough iterations to bound the rate.

candidates.name: Extract python3 heredocs from build-review-packet.sh
candidates.fit_for_gap: goal-3 fix (conditional): build-review-packet.sh (919 lines, verified by wc -l this session) embeds ~10 python3 heredoc programs — the construct that hung indefinitely in other scripts on this host and was fixed by extraction; never extracted here.
candidates.decision_rationale: CONDITIONAL on cand-2 isolating the hang inside build-review-packet.sh's python3 heredocs: extract them to standalone .py files following the repo's proven extraction pattern (see analysis.md Appendix A for the verifiable .sh/.py companion list in skills/research/deep-research/scripts/). Do NOT extract pre-emptively: Goal 4 requires an adversarially reviewed diagnosis before any fix is written, and a standalone full deep run completed through this script in <60 s (assessment) — the heredocs are a lead, not a confirmed cause. Verdict 'adapt' = apply the repo-internal pattern, gated on diagnosis.

evidence.claim: Popen with PIPE deadlocks when data exceeds the OS pipe buffer without concurrent draining; use communicate().
subprocess hangs indefinitely when stdout exceeds ~65000 chars.
Pipe deadlock occurs at the ~64 KB OS pipe-buffer boundary; timing-dependent.

risks: Mechanism (pipe-buffer deadlock) fits the intermittency but the hang site is unconfirmed; if the harness isolates elsewhere (write-provenance.sh, judge dispatch), this candidate is void.
Whether the ~64 KB threshold is actually crossed at stage-10 input sizes is unmeasured; harness must capture output volume at the hang site.
